names: P27 -- oval running track and field (south of UCSF Medical Center)
summary: A real oval running track with a central grass field, just south of the UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay campus; identified via this project's owner-directed real-gap-fragment method from satellite imagery, not a surveyed footprint or a named park record. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P27' among the parcels RPD 'will manage ... when built,' i.e. not yet complete as of that date; this project's own satellite check found it already built by September 2026. Name and operator not confirmed by any source found.

milestones.text: Not yet built: OCII's Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P27' among the parcels RPD will manage "when built," distinct from the already-managed parcels listed alongside it
Confirmed already built (oval track, central field and surrounding path clearly visible) during this project's own satellite-imagery review

images.credit: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Farm Service Agency, NAIP aerial imagery (2024 flight), via USDA's 'latest NAIP' image service
images.license_note: USDA's data.gov catalog record for NAIP imagery sets the license to the U.S. government public-domain label (usa.gov/publicdomain/label/1.0); the USDA FSA policies page says public-domain information may be freely distributed with credit requested ('U.S. Department of Agriculture, Farm Service Agency'). Read 2026-09-22.
images.caption: USDA NAIP aerial orthophoto (2024 flight), cropped to the Mission Bay project area and its immediate surroundings
images.appeal_note: A straight-down orthophoto rather than an oblique aerial, but Oracle Park and Chase Center are both clearly recognizable landmarks in the frame, giving anyone who knows the city an immediate fix on the neighborhood.

images.credit: Firstcultural (Alfred Twu), aerial view from a departing flight, via Wikimedia Commons; CC0; downscaled to 1600 px
images.license_note: Wikimedia Commons' license box on the file page confirms CC0 (public domain dedication) by Firstcultural (Alfred Twu). Read 2026-09-23.
images.caption: Aerial view of Mission Bay, Oracle Park and the Caltrain/King Street area from a departing flight
images.appeal_note: Oracle Park's diamond and Chase Center's dome (with its own logo) are both clearly identifiable landmarks in one colorful frame -- reads far better at card size than the flatter government orthophoto.

sources.title: Mission Bay Parks Open Space (CAC Item 2, September 2023)

open_questions: No source pins down exactly when construction happened between the Sept 2023 'not yet built' status and this project's own Sept 2026 satellite confirmation that it exists; a three-year window, not a single date.
Name and operator not confirmed by any source found; this project's own digitization_method log notes it sits south of the hospital campus, bounded by real streets on all sides.

Whether OCII's own current numbering scheme still uses 'P27' for exactly this footprint was not independently confirmed on OCII's current public Mission Bay South open-space page, which does not list a P27 among the parcels it names (P1, P2, P3, P5, P6, P26).
